chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Hammad ibn 'Uthman who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mufrad (one who performs Hajj al-Mufrad): does he hasten his Tawaf or delay it? He said, 'It is the same by Allah, whether he hastens it or delays it.'
As for the Tawaf of women, it is not permissible except after returning from Mina, with the choice (to do so then). He narrated that.

key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: Hajj al-Mufrad (a type of Hajj where the pilgrim enters Ihram for Hajj only, without Umrah)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina (a valley and site near Mecca)

ai.seo_question: When should a Mufrad perform Tawaf during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of Tawaf al-Ifadah for the Mufrad, affirming that delaying or hastening the circumambation is equally valid, a ruling that underscores the ease (*rukhsah*) in Hajj rituals. It further specifies that for women, the performance of this Tawaf is contingent upon returning from Mina, highlighting a practical distinction in the sequence of rites. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the non-mandatory nature of the specific timing of Tawaf al-Ifadah, provided the pilgrim completes it before the final departure from Mecca.
